question: Will Trump have formally nominated a permanent Secretary of the Army by September 18, 2026?

calls.reasoning: As of 2026-09-08 the Army secretary post is vacant (Driscoll out Sept 2; Telle acting since Sept 3) and no pick has been decided — Semafor Sept 2 says Parnell 'doesn't have the nod locked down yet' and it is 'unclear when' Trump will nominate; the WH offered no timeline. YES requires a decision plus formal transmittal to the Senate within ~10 days. Reference class of service-secretary vacancies (Army 2017/2019, Navy 2017, Air Force 2019, 2025 Trump-term picks) shows vacancy-to-formal-transmittal lags of 1-6 months, with no instance clearing ~2.5 weeks from an undecided vacancy; FBI background checks and OGE ethics agreements alone usually take weeks after the pick is public. The one real YES path is Trump naming an already-vetted, Senate-confirmed insider (Telle, Parnell, Derrick Anderson) whose paperwork could be recycled fast, which keeps this above ~3% rather than near zero. No prediction market prices this event on Polymarket, Manifold, or Kalshi, so there is no crowd anchor. Announcements of intent explicitly do not count, which further narrows YES.
calls.reference_class: US service-secretary (Army/Navy/Air Force) vacancies since 1990 where the incumbent departed with no successor announced — fraction where a formal nomination reached the Senate within ~16 days of the departure
